scene.label: Act 1, Scene 6
scene.title: SCENE VI. The same. Before the Castle.

content.text: Enter Duncan, Malcolm, Donalbain, Banquo, Lennox, Macduff, Ross, Angus and Attendants.

lines.text: This castle hath a pleasant seat. The air
lines.plainText: This castle hath a pleasant seat The air

lines.text: Nimbly and sweetly recommends itself
lines.plainText: Nimbly and sweetly recommends itself

lines.text: Unto our gentle senses.
lines.plainText: Unto our gentle senses

lines.text: This guest of summer,
lines.plainText: This guest of summer

lines.text: The temple-haunting martlet, does approve,
lines.plainText: The templehaunting martlet does approve

lines.text: By his loved mansionry, that the heaven's breath
lines.plainText: By his loved mansionry that the heaven's breath

lines.text: Smells wooingly here: no jutty, frieze,
lines.plainText: Smells wooingly here no jutty frieze

lines.text: Buttress, nor coign of vantage, but this bird
lines.plainText: Buttress nor coign of vantage but this bird

lines.text: hath made his pendant bed and procreant cradle.
lines.plainText: hath made his pendant bed and procreant cradle

lines.text: Where they most breed and haunt, I have observ'd
lines.plainText: Where they most breed and haunt I have observ'd

lines.text: The air is delicate.
lines.plainText: The air is delicate

lines.text: See, see, our honour'd hostess!—
lines.plainText: See see our honour'd hostess

lines.text: The love that follows us sometime is our trouble,
lines.plainText: The love that follows us sometime is our trouble

lines.text: Which still we thank as love. Herein I teach you
lines.plainText: Which still we thank as love Herein I teach you

lines.text: How you shall bid God 'ild us for your pains,
lines.plainText: How you shall bid God 'ild us for your pains

lines.text: And thank us for your trouble.
lines.plainText: And thank us for your trouble

lines.text: All our service,
lines.plainText: All our service

lines.text: In every point twice done, and then done double,
lines.plainText: In every point twice done and then done double

lines.text: Were poor and single business to contend
lines.plainText: Were poor and single business to contend

lines.text: Against those honours deep and broad wherewith
lines.plainText: Against those honours deep and broad wherewith

lines.text: Your Majesty loads our house: for those of old,
lines.plainText: Your Majesty loads our house for those of old

lines.text: And the late dignities heap'd up to them,
lines.plainText: And the late dignities heap'd up to them

lines.text: We rest your hermits.
lines.plainText: We rest your hermits

lines.text: Where's the Thane of Cawdor?
lines.plainText: Where's the Thane of Cawdor

lines.text: We cours'd him at the heels, and had a purpose
lines.plainText: We cours'd him at the heels and had a purpose

lines.text: To be his purveyor: but he rides well;
lines.plainText: To be his purveyor but he rides well

lines.text: And his great love, sharp as his spur, hath holp him
lines.plainText: And his great love sharp as his spur hath holp him

lines.text: To his home before us. Fair and noble hostess,
lines.plainText: To his home before us Fair and noble hostess

lines.text: We are your guest tonight.
lines.plainText: We are your guest tonight

lines.text: Your servants ever
lines.plainText: Your servants ever

lines.text: Have theirs, themselves, and what is theirs, in compt,
lines.plainText: Have theirs themselves and what is theirs in compt

lines.text: To make their audit at your Highness' pleasure,
lines.plainText: To make their audit at your Highness' pleasure

lines.text: Still to return your own.
lines.plainText: Still to return your own

lines.text: Give me your hand;
lines.plainText: Give me your hand

lines.text: Conduct me to mine host: we love him highly,
lines.plainText: Conduct me to mine host we love him highly

lines.text: And shall continue our graces towards him.
lines.plainText: And shall continue our graces towards him

lines.text: By your leave, hostess.
lines.plainText: By your leave hostess
